title: Consumer-Level and Per-Account Holds in Hardship and Protective Holds
content:
For Hardship and Protective Holds, how far one request reaches across a consumer's placed accounts depends on the tier. The desk applies the following rule.

## The rule

For tiers whose one approved request places a hold on every open eligible account of the consumer — the Disaster Relief Hold and the Military Service Hold — one request from the consumer is recorded as a hold on every open placed account of that consumer that the tier can hold, all with the same request date and the same documentation reference, and they are decided together on the same evidence; an account the tier cannot hold is simply left out. For every other tier the consumer names the accounts, and each named account is a separate request decided on its own records.

Hold-day limits are never pooled across accounts: the hold days counted in the rolling 12 months and the grants counted in the rolling 12 months are counted per placed account, so a consumer with three accounts can hold all three for the full tier length at the same time. The limits that apply to a hold are those of its own tier; days of tiers whose days do not count toward the annual limit are not counted against any tier.

## The two patterns side by side

| | Consumer-level tiers (Disaster Relief Hold, Military Service Hold) | All other tiers |
|---|---|---|
| Which accounts the request covers | Every open placed account of the consumer that the tier can hold | Only the accounts the consumer names |
| Request date and documentation reference | The same on every account covered | Each request has its own |
| How the request is decided | Together, on the same evidence | Each account separately, on its own records |
| An account the tier cannot hold | Simply left out | Not part of the request unless named; decided on its own records if named |

## Limits per account

- The rolling 12-month hold days and the rolling 12-month grants are each counted on one placed account at a time; they are never added up across the consumer's accounts.
- A hold is measured against the limits of its own tier.
- Days of a tier whose days do not count toward the annual limit are not counted against any tier, whichever tier is later requested on that account.

## Worked illustration (hypothetical)

A consumer owes three placed accounts and asks for a Military Service Hold. All three accounts are open and each is one the tier can hold. Because the tier is consumer-level, the one request is recorded as a hold on all three accounts, all bearing the same request date and orders reference, and they are decided together. Each held account then counts its own hold days and grants; the hold on one account uses nothing of the limits of the other.

A second consumer with three accounts asks for a Documented Hardship Hold and names two of them. Two separate requests are recorded, each decided on its own account's records; the third account is not part of the request.
